source_read: PDF, online-first article pp. 1-11 (PDFs/MDMA/Earleywine_2025_QuestionsAndConcerns.pdf): read in full, including Tables 1 and 2, the Appendix (vignette and prompts), funding, disclosure, data availability and references; all 11 pages rendered at 110 dpi (Tables 1-2 and the Discussion's paragraph breaks checked on the images). Crossref records of MAPP1 and MAPP2 read in my own browser tab to check reporting issue 4. Step 1 (blind extraction) not run this round, per the round brief.

design.note: Qualitative story-completion study of 30 veterans; reader 28 is right that it is not a commentary. The background statements about the trials and the FDA are second-hand and correctly kept apart.

key_findings.note: p. 3, left column: PCL-5 19-65 (43.67, 10.91), 26 of 30 above 31-33, alpha 0.86, omega 0.85; PHQ-9 8-21 (14.70, 3.74), alpha 0.53, omega indeterminate.

Every frequency matches Table 1 (pp. 4-5). Note for use: Hope's 20 (67%) counts 18 stories with reasonable positive hopes and 2 that allude to having little hope (the code's own definition); the Discussion says 'hope ... (or a lack of hope; 67%)'.

Checked against Table 2 cell by cell: Retrauma -0.425 under Willing, Side Effects -0.384 under Familiar, Skeptical -0.699 and -0.376, Neophobic 0.344 under PCL-5; word-count column 0.323, 0.499, 0.331, 0.365, 0.468, 0.405, 0.451.
The 2nd paragraph of the Introduction begins at the foot of the left column; the d values are in the right column.
Sources as stated: the rejection is cited to Marks (2024, JAMA), the concerns to Jacobs (2024) and Jarow (2024a, 2024b); 'split vote' carries no citation of its own.
4th Discussion paragraph, the one beginning 'Based on these new data' (p. 6, right column).
The 7th Discussion paragraph begins at the foot of the left column of p. 7 and ends at the top of the right column.

reporting_issues.note: Table 1 lists 27 coded themes plus the two ratings; Microdosing (4) and Skeptical (no frequency given anywhere) are missing; the capitalization note does not match Table 2's rows.
Table 2: Microdosing 0.313 under Lifetime Drug, Wrong Information 0.339 under Current Drug; the text puts both under lifetime use.
Table 2 has no PHQ-9 column and no Hope row; the Discussion's 'treatment outcome research' has no counterpart in the word-count column.

Checked in Crossref: MAPP1 is 27(6):1025-1033 with Doblin 38th of 38 authors (third in Earleywine's list); MAPP2 is 29(10):2473-2480, titled 'a randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial'. Madero and Alvarez (2023, p. 20) independently print MAPP1 as 27(6):1025-1033.
The next sentence's citations (Penn and Yehuda, 2023; Zamaria et al., 2025) concern knowledge gaps, not the FDA.

risk_of_bias.note: I agree with every domain and the overall; two notes below.

domains.domain: Research design appropriate to the question

domains.note: The vignette's opening line (a big research project suggesting MDMA helps) is the strongest lean, besides the hope prompt (Appendix, p. 11).

Borderline with high: besides the text-table disagreements and the four codes kept below reliability, codes are declared orthogonal because chi-square tests gave no p < .001 (p. 3), an unusual criterion among many tests, and Table 2 shows no code-code correlations to support the Discussion's statement that the codes did not correlate with one another.
The closing inference also contradicts the paper's own earlier statement (see 'missed').

overall.note: Some concerns; no domain is high.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor for the study's own findings. Two additions in the Discussion, outside the abstract: psychoeducation materials are to 'emphasize that this treatment helped PTSD patients who did not respond to other interventions' (p. 7, 5th paragraph), an efficacy statement without a citation; and the closing sentence's claim for targeted information contradicts p. 6 (see 'missed'). In results_show, 'Most stories voiced hope (20 of 30)' should read 'Hope came up in 20 of 30 stories (18 with positive hopes, 2 alluding to little hope)'.

missed: Internal contradiction: the Discussion's 3rd paragraph (p. 6) concludes that targeted information seems less necessary than brief, broad psychoeducation, while the last sentence of the paper (p. 8) says the results suggest that targeted information can increase veterans' understanding. Worth adding to reporting issue 6's family or to the interpretation gap.
Hope's frequency (20, 67%) includes 2 stories coded -1 (little hope): Table 1's definition gives 2, 10, 18 and 0 occurrences for -1, 0, 1 and 2.
Further unsourced background statements: the 2017 Breakthrough Therapy status (p. 1) and the psychoeducation line that the treatment helped patients who did not respond to other interventions (p. 7).

The Introduction also cites a cost model by authors with declared ties to the sponsor (Marseille, Mitchell and Kahn, 2022; the ties are declared in marseille_2025) for improved cost-effectiveness and the elimination of premature deaths (p. 1), without its assumptions. Not needed for any claim; a pointer for the cost claim's statement that no independent economic evaluation is among the sources.
